headline: Sequential rebound, but earnings still trail last year
summary_short: ConocoPhillips reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $15.76B (-4.6% y/y, +17.7% q/q) and diluted EPS of $1.78, up 52.1% from a weak prior quarter but down 20.2% y/y as lower production and softer gas realizations weighed on results.
summary_long: Revenue of $15.76B fell 4.6% y/y as production declined 80 MBOED (3%) to 2,309 MBOED on normal field decline, partly offset by new wells; realized gas prices fell 27% to $4.09/mcf while crude realizations rose to $73.47/bbl. Operating income of $3.39B (-19.7% y/y) reflected weaker realizations and $160M higher DD&A from Marathon Oil purchase-price allocations, partly offset by $230M lower production and operating expense. Diluted EPS of $1.78 fell 20.2% y/y but rose 52.1% from a weak prior quarter. Operating cash flow of $4.3B (-29.8% y/y) reflected receivable timing and lower prices; the company returned $2.0B to shareholders ($1.0B buybacks, $1.0B dividend) and held $5.9B cash. ConocoPhillips lowered full-year production guidance to 2.295-2.325 MMBOED (ex-Qatar); capex guidance unchanged at $12-12.5B.

drivers.explanation: Lower produced volumes (-$420M) and lower realized natural gas/NGL prices (-$537M), partly offset by higher crude and bitumen prices (+$243M).

Segment declines: Lower 48 on lower realized prices and higher DD&A; Canada on Surmont royalty increase and a contingent-consideration fair-value loss; EMENA on lower volumes/prices and tax-mix shift.
Operating income fell 19.7% y/y against a smaller 4.6% revenue decline, so margin compression is arithmetic: costs (notably DD&A) grew as a share of a shrinking revenue base.
Company states the decrease resulted from receivable timing, lower production and lower realized commodity prices.
Normal field decline across segments, partly offset by new wells online in the Lower 48, Canada, Alaska, China, Australia and Libya; ex-portfolio-changes production fell 1% y/y.

Results rebounded sequentially from a weak prior quarter but remained below last year; the company also lowered full-year production guidance to exclude Qatar and reflect a higher Surmont royalty rate, while capex and cost guidance held.
